rationale: Verified 3 critical security/correctness bypasses in tool-call confirmation (request-override hard-ceiling bypass, multi-tool-call confirm-shows-one-executes-all, cross-assistant resume with no ownership check), plus a floor-policy AttributeError that crashes every request once a customer configures min_tool_call_policy. Diff is oversized (diff_metadata.oversized) so coverage of the ~106-file, ~18k-line change is necessarily partial; standards audit found commit-format and code-quality violations (coverage_gap=false, so treated as complete for the sampled scope) and flagged them blocking. 2 decision_needed items record real spec-vs-code conflicts (out-of-scope Conversation.tool_call_policy column; an unexplained, unrelated teamsBotIntegration flag flip in shared customer-config.yaml) that need author/PM input, not a unilateral fix. Two lens-reported crashes (jira _http_method_is_safe import, workspace tools glob/prefix NameError) were confirmed already fixed in the working tree and are dismissed along with 10 other lens findings (dead code, stale docs, unreached defensive-guard asymmetries, and is_safe() coverage that was verified correct on inspection); 0 findings deferred as pre-existing.

AC3 - Allow executes the requested tool call
business_review.notes: resume_from_interrupt() resumes the graph past the interrupt

business_review.notes: denies ALL tool_calls in the batch even though only the first was ever shown to the user - see CR-006

business_review.notes: Postgres-backed checkpoint reloaded by conversation_id on resume

business_review.notes: allow/deny both stream a normal completion afterward

business_review.notes: interrupted Thought rendered with aborted/interrupted flags

business_review.notes: InMemorySaver + thread_id='thread' fallback preserved; feature-flag gate forces AUTO_APPROVE when disabled

business_review.notes: field defined on StreamedGenerationResult but never assigned anywhere in src/codemie; actual signal is an unrelated Thought object

implemented instead as tool_call_policy:ToolCallPolicy enum + allow_override:bool; functionally equivalent, different contract shape

business_review.notes: user param and pending_tool_call_id echo both dropped from the implemented signatures; extensibility/validation hooks missing
interrupt_before wiring, non-confirmation fallback, checkpoint columns/saver/service, resume_allow/deny mechanism, GET conversation exposure, configure_agent_kwargs wiring all match the design

standards_review.notes: several commits in range use no ticket prefix ('checkpoint 2', 'docs: ...') or conventional type(scope) syntax instead of the documented 'EPMCDME-####: Description' format
new tool_confirmation/tool_permissions modules use typing.Optional[X] and omit 'from __future__ import annotations', against the documented convention for new modules
sampled is_safe()/http-method classification fails closed; migrations form a consistent single-line chain; no credential logging found in files opened

findings.title: make run no longer starts the app
findings.problem: The `run:` target was changed from `poetry run uvicorn codemie.rest_api.main:app --host=0.0.0.0 --port=8080 --reload` to bare `poetry run uvicorn`. A companion `[tool.uvicorn]` block was added to pyproject.toml, but the standard uvicorn CLI does not read app/host/port/reload from pyproject.toml without an explicit config mechanism.
findings.impact: `make run` breaks local server startup for every developer following the documented workflow; this is unrelated to the tool-call-confirmation feature and ships as unexplained scope creep.
findings.recommendation: Restore the explicit `poetry run uvicorn codemie.rest_api.main:app --host=0.0.0.0 --port=8080 --reload` invocation, or verify (and prove via a working `make run`) that the new pyproject.toml block is actually consumed before relying on it.

findings.title: Unrelated teamsBotIntegration flag flipped off
findings.problem: `features:teamsBotIntegration.enabled` is flipped from `true` to `false` in the same diff that adds `features:tool_permissions`, with no mention anywhere in the change's own scope or documentation.
findings.impact: This is a shared customer-facing config default; disabling it as an apparently accidental side effect of an unrelated feature branch risks silently turning off Teams Bot integration in production for any customer relying on the default config.
findings.recommendation: Revert this line unless the flip is independently confirmed intentional by the change author/PM; if intentional, split it into its own reviewed commit with its own justification.

findings.title: New chat message silently wipes a pending confirmation
findings.problem: `LangGraphAgent.stream()` unconditionally calls `ConversationCheckpointService().clear(self.conversation_id)` at the start of every run whenever `require_tool_confirmation` is true. No code path checks for or blocks a fresh (non-resume) chat request on a conversation that already has a genuinely pending tool-call confirmation.
findings.impact: If a user (or a retried client) sends a new message to the same conversation while an earlier tool-call confirmation is still awaiting a decision, this clears the in-flight checkpoint and pending_tool_call, silently discarding the interrupt instead of rejecting the new request or queuing behind the pending confirmation.
findings.recommendation: Before clearing, check `ConversationCheckpointService().get_pending_tool_call(conversation_id)`; if one exists, reject the new chat request (e.g. 409) instead of overwriting the pending state.

findings.title: Unbounded recursion on APPROVE_FOR_ME auto-resume
findings.problem: When `tool_call_policy=APPROVE_FOR_ME` and every tool call in a step is judged safe, `_stream_graph` recurses into itself (`return self._stream_graph(None, config, chunks_collector)`) once per auto-approved step, with no depth counter or iteration cap.
findings.impact: A model that repeatedly emits consecutive safe tool calls under APPROVE_FOR_ME grows the Python call stack unbounded until it hits `RecursionError`, crashing the agent thread instead of completing the run.
findings.recommendation: Convert the auto-resume branch into an explicit loop (or add a bounded recursion/iteration counter) so an arbitrarily long chain of safe tool calls cannot exhaust the call stack.

findings.title: New tool-confirmation modules violate documented typing convention
findings.problem: code-quality.md's Types And Imports standard requires `X | None` unions/parameterized generics plus `from __future__ import annotations` in new modules; `models.py`, `conversation_checkpoint_saver.py`, `service/tool_permissions_service.py` and `service/conversation_checkpoint_service.py` instead import and use `typing.Optional[X]` throughout with no future-annotations import.
findings.impact: Violates a documented blocking standard for new code across four of this change's core new modules.
findings.recommendation: Replace `Optional[X]` with `X | None` in these four files, or add `from __future__ import annotations` if `Optional` must stay for a runtime reason.

findings.title: Allow on a multi-tool-call turn executes calls the user never saw
findings.problem: `ask_for_tool_confirmation` builds the confirmation dialog (`ToolCallPendingEvent`) from only `tool_calls[0]` (`tool_call = tool_calls[0]`), even though `all_tool_call_ids` records every tool call id in the AI turn. When the user presses Allow, `resume_from_interrupt` resumes the entire interrupted LangGraph step, which executes *every* tool call in that step, not just the one shown.
findings.impact: If the model emits multiple tool calls in one turn and only the first happens to be shown as 'safe-looking', the user's Allow on that single dialog silently also executes any sibling tool calls in the same batch - including unreviewed, potentially mutating ones - defeating the purpose of per-call confirmation. This is a direct confirmation-bypass path for a mutating action.
findings.recommendation: Either surface every tool call in the pending confirmation UI and require a decision on the whole batch, or gate execution so only tool calls the user actually reviewed are allowed to proceed (denying/re-queuing the rest).

findings.title: reject_tool_call(None) leaves the streaming response open
findings.problem: `reject_tool_call` returns immediately when `pending is None`, without closing `self.thread_generator`. `handle_tool_call_resume` (assistant_handlers.py) fetches `pending` once via `ConversationCheckpointService().get_pending_tool_call(...)` before opening the `StreamingResponse`, and the router's own pre-check (`_resume_tool_call`) that the checkpoint exists is not atomic with that fetch - a concurrent resume for the same conversation can clear the checkpoint in between.
findings.impact: On that race, a deny action calls `reject_tool_call(None)`, which returns without ever closing the thread generator, so the client's StreamingResponse never receives a terminating chunk and hangs open until client-side disconnect/timeout.
findings.recommendation: In `reject_tool_call`, close `self.thread_generator` (and/or send a terminal error chunk) before returning when `pending is None`, mirroring the guard already used elsewhere in this mixin.

findings.title: Conversation.tool_call_policy contradicts stated out-of-scope
findings.problem: Design 2026-08-10 explicitly lists 'no changes to POST v1/conversations or the conversation entity' as out of scope, but this change adds a persisted `tool_call_policy` column to `Conversation` (migration `v4w5x6y7z8a9_add_tool_call_policy_to_conversations.py`) and a `tool_call_policy` field on `UpdateConversationRequest`.
findings.impact: Either the later spec addendum was meant to supersede this column and it should not have been added, or the addendum is stale and the column is legitimate - the two design documents disagree and the code picked a side without recording the decision anywhere.
findings.recommendation: Confirm with the design owner whether per-conversation tool_call_policy persistence is still wanted; if not, remove the column/migration/field, otherwise update the 08-10 addendum to reflect that this scope boundary was revised.

findings.title: Tool-call resume has no assistant/conversation ownership check
findings.problem: `resume_tool_call` checks the caller's READ access to `assistant_id` from the URL, and `handle_tool_call_resume` separately checks WRITE access to the conversation looked up by `request.conversation_id` - but nothing verifies that `conversation_id` actually belongs to `assistant_id`. The handler then calls `AssistantService.build_agent(assistant=self.assistant, ...)` using the URL's assistant while resuming the unrelated conversation's pending checkpoint/tool call.
findings.impact: A user with WRITE access to their own conversation under a strict assistant A1, and READ access to an unrelated (e.g. shared/public) assistant A2 with a laxer tool_call_policy, can call the endpoint with `assistant_id=A2` and `conversation_id=<A1's conversation>`. The pending tool call originally gated under A1's stricter policy gets resumed inside an agent built with A2's configuration - a cross-resource authorization/config-confusion bypass for a mutating action.
findings.recommendation: Before resuming, verify the conversation's own assistant_id(s) include the URL's assistant_id (or otherwise resolve the agent from the conversation's actual assistant, not the URL's), and reject the request otherwise.

findings.title: Request override fully replaces the assistant's confirmation requirement
findings.problem: When `base.allow_override` is true (the default for a new `ToolPermissionsConfig`, per `allow_override: bool = True`), `effective_policy = tool_call_policy_override or conversation_policy or base.tool_call_policy` lets a per-request `tool_call_policy` (e.g. `AUTO_APPROVE`) fully replace a stricter assistant-configured policy (e.g. `ASK_FOR_APPROVAL`), confirmed by the project's own `test_request_override_beats_assistant`.
findings.impact: Design 08-10's priority rule states the assistant-level confirmation requirement is a hard ceiling the request flag cannot disable. As implemented, any caller who can set `tool_call_policy` on a chat request can unilaterally downgrade a mutating-tool-requiring assistant to auto-approve, bypassing confirmation for a mutating action entirely.
findings.recommendation: Change the resolution so a request/conversation override can only raise strictness above the assistant's configured policy, never lower it (e.g. `ToolCallPolicy.stricter(base.tool_call_policy, tool_call_policy_override or conversation_policy or base.tool_call_policy)`), consistent with how the customer floor is already applied a few lines below.

findings.title: Customer floor policy crashes when configured (raw string, not enum)
findings.problem: `floor_policy = customer_config.get_feature_setting(self._TOOL_PERMISSIONS_FEATURE, self._TOOL_CALL_POLICY_SETTING)` returns the raw YAML string (confirmed by `test_tool_permissions_loaded_with_floor` returning `'ask_for_approval'`), which is then passed directly into `ToolCallPolicy.stricter(floor_policy, effective_policy)`. `stricter` accesses `a.strictness`, a property that only exists on `ToolCallPolicy` enum members, not `str`.
findings.impact: Any customer that configures `features:tool_permissions.min_tool_call_policy` in customer-config.yaml raises `AttributeError` on every chat request that reaches `get_effective_permissions`, breaking chat entirely for that tenant - the exact configuration path this feature is built to support.
findings.recommendation: Coerce the setting to the enum before use, e.g. `floor_policy = ToolCallPolicy(floor_policy) if floor_policy else None`, and cover it with a test that goes through `customer_config.get_feature_setting` for real rather than mocking it to already return an enum.

findings.title: Commit history violates the documented ticket-format standard
findings.problem: git-workflow.md requires commit subjects in the form 'EPMCDME-####: Description'. The review range includes 'checkpoint 2' (no ticket, no colon), 'docs: add spec for per-request require_confirmation flag' (no ticket prefix), and numerous 'feat(EPMCDME-13903): ...'/'fix(EPMCDME-13903): ...'/'refactor(EPMCDME-13903): ...' subjects using conventional-commit type(scope) syntax instead.
findings.impact: A large fraction of this change's own commit history breaks the documented commit-message-format standard the standards audit enforces as blocking.
findings.recommendation: Reword or squash the non-conforming commits to 'EPMCDME-13903: <description>' before merge.
